description: Single source of truth for AutoFlow's per-phase spawn policy (model + effort). Read it with scripts/spawn-policy/spawn-policy.sh; never restate its values in prose (CLAUDE.md > Spawn Model — Phase-by-Phase).
sample_contract: This file is a SAMPLE carrying the values currently applied, not a universal vocabulary the framework enforces. It ships as a `scaffold` artifact: a stamp/install creates it only when absent and never overwrites it (not even under --force), so the values here are the target's to configure at stamp time and afterwards. On a version bump, run `scripts/spawn-policy/spawn-policy.sh check` and add any newly required row — the drift detector's D6 leg (issue #185) runs that check and the required-row comparison against the clone's sample at /autoflow:install and PREFLIGHT, so a stale scaffold is reported there with the rows to fix; an outdated scaffold is a diagnosable state, since both deliberation workflows fail closed on a missing required workflow_sites row (issue #166 renamed the architect deliberation's rows to dev-turn / test-turn / scribe / ledger and removed deliberation_caps; issue #179 moved the discussion turns out of the workflow — the architect-deliberation site rows are now scribe / ledger only, and the two participants are direct spawns governed by the new phases rows architect-dev-participant / architect-test-participant — a target still carrying the former rows or lacking the new ones fails closed at its next ARCHITECT until this file is updated). `check` reads the agent definitions from `.claude/agents/` when it holds autoflow-*.md files, otherwise from the installed plugin's agents/ (resolved via scripts/lib/plugin-root.sh: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT in a hook, the harness registries under ~/.claude/plugins in a plain shell) — a thin-root target has only the plugin copy; `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=<plugin dir>` points it there explicitly. Issue #180 made every effort value explicit (coding and judgment roles xhigh, analysis high, the ledger sites low) so a spawn's effort no longer follows the operator's session setting, and gave the loop check its own shipped definition `autoflow-loopcheck` in place of the harness `Explore` type — a target still carrying `agent_type: Explore` on `diagnose-loopcheck` keeps working (the hook admits Explore as a research type) but cannot pin that row's effort until it adopts the new type. A phases[].effort is not a target-side lever: it must equal the `effort:` frontmatter line of the definition the target actually loads (the plugin's, on a thin-root target) and `check` fails closed otherwise — see effort_contract.phase_effort_ownership; a target that needs a different direct-spawn effort changes the shipped definition, not this row. workflow_sites effort stays target-configurable.

effort_contract.is_the_vocabulary_check_applies: `scripts/spawn-policy/spawn-policy.sh check` reads its admitted effort vocabulary and its inherit sentinel from THIS object, so `check` is a self-consistency check over one source. A runtime with a different effort vocabulary is accommodated by editing this contract, never by patching the checker; model values are deliberately unvalidated beyond presence and shape
effort_contract.admitted_one_spelling_per_level: both harness channels run the same coercion, which also accepts the alias "med" for "medium"; this policy admits one spelling per level, so "med" is deliberately not admitted here
effort_contract.sentinel_is_config_only: "inherit" is this file's own vocabulary and is never written to either harness channel: a Workflow agent() opts object omits the effort key, and an agent-definition frontmatter omits the effort line
effort_contract.absent_means: identical to "inherit" — the row declares no override and the spawn inherits the session effort. A row carrying no effort key at all is a validation error, not an inherit: `spawn-policy.sh check` rejects it, so a misspelled key surfaces in the tree rather than reading as policy
effort_contract.phase_effort_ownership: A phases[] row's effort is DELIVERED by the agent definition's `effort:` frontmatter line, not by this file: the harness reads a direct spawn's effort from the definition it loads, and the Agent tool carries `model` per call but no effort. The definitions are versioned tool source (a thin-root target loads the installed plugin's agents/), so phase-row effort is fixed per plugin version and is not a per-target lever; this file's phases[].effort is the projection source at the tool repository and must equal the loaded definition's line — `check` fails closed on a mismatch (issue #180, PR #183 review). Only workflow_sites effort reaches its spawn from this file at run time and is configurable per target. A harness research type (Explore / Plan / claude-code-guide) ships no definition at all, so a row that uses one admits the inherit sentinel only; `check` refuses a concrete effort there. The projection is recognised in one canonical spelling only — `effort: <value>` at column 0 of the first YAML block, unquoted, no trailing comment; any other spelling a YAML parser could read as that key — including an indented key, since a mapping indented as a whole is still the same mapping — is refused by `check`, since the checker carries no YAML parser and does not guess. The block itself is accepted in block style only — one plain `key: value` per line at column 0, blank lines and `#` comments; a flow mapping, an explicit key, a merge key or a multi-line scalar is refused as a shape, before any "no effort line means inherit" verdict.

diagnose-intake-triage.work_type: new-issue readiness pre-filter (planning/design/ADR prerequisite), no code tools

diagnose-loopcheck.work_type: review-response loop check — prior-cycle complaint-class comparison (issue #180: a shipped read-only definition replaces the harness Explore type so the row's effort projects into agent frontmatter)

diagnose-phase-3.work_type: necessity scoring (Behavior gap + Code-change lever; reuse-neutral)

architect-dev-participant.work_type: ARCHITECT relay participant, Developer AI side — one persistent spawn per discussion, woken by agent ID for each of its turns (ADR-0023 D2); feature design under the Discussion Protocol

architect-test-participant.work_type: ARCHITECT relay participant, Test AI side — one persistent spawn per discussion, woken by agent ID for each of its turns (ADR-0023 D2); verification design under the Discussion Protocol

red.work_type: acceptance criteria → test code; test doubles re-derived from the real types and response shapes (tier reverted on issue #180 — record: CLAUDE.md > Spawn Model > Revert history)

green.work_type: minimum implementation that passes the tests

audit.work_type: security rubric, 5 items × 10 points (tier raised on issue #180 — 23 rubric-covered findings escaped to the configured reviewer across four repositories, 17 of them cross-tenant / cross-org boundary violations)

handoff-review-triage.work_type: reviewer-comment ingestion (severity classification) + Low-finding impact judgment
